text: So every Thursday around 2pm, in the milk crate by the backdoor, Imre finds something in it that is not milk, something else. First week, its a Field Guide to Mushrooms of the Northeast, has the Carver Street Library stamp on the flyleaf, due date long past. Second week, same book. Third week, same. He stopped reshelving it in his head. It lives on the flour bench now, between the scale and the rye starter tub, cover gone soft with dough dusted thumbprints. Tonight, he slid the crate out with his hip, hands still in oven mitts, and the book was there again, heavier than usual. A square of yellow paper stuck out near page 112. He peeled the mitts off. The note was in pencil, small, slanted hard right. It said, your door smells better than the library. I keep meaning to bring it to the right place. Is the morel on this page the one you use? T. Imre looked at the page. Nothing circled, morel sat there, wrinkled brown. He took the pencil from behind his ear, flipped the note, wrote: No. Never used one. Then after a moment, he added: Come at five, there's bread. Pressed it back in.
